scenario: Scenario 1: Snapshot manifest count exceeds the regions a restore produces
notes: The real system threw QuotaExceededException from the target's throw statement for a restore that fits the quota, using public Admin calls and no fault. In the headline path (MC-1) the guard adds the unfiltered snapshot manifest size, which includes a split parent or the MOB pseudo-region, while the namespace cache counts neither: at quota 10, a 9-region table is split (cache 10), snapshotted (11 entries), disabled and restored, so the guard computes 10 - 10 + 11 = 11 > 10, although the restored table has 10 regions. The stack frame reports line 133 because the throw statement spans lines 130-133 and its constructor call maps to the last line; the compiled line table shows new at line 130 and invokespecial under line 133, and this is the only throw in that method (repro/MC-6.javap.txt). The mechanism and scenario fields describe MC-1 only, a no-fault branch of the count logic. All 16 hunt configs violated TargetSafe, and all 8 findings (MC-1 to MC-8) reproduced the same throw under the Phase 4 rules: MC-2 and MC-3 need no fault (BRANCH), MC-4 needs a master failover (RESTART), MC-5 and MC-8 need a master crash during a procedure (RESTART, with INTERLEAVING against the rebuild scan), MC-6 needs a split failure (FAULT), and MC-7 needs a clone racing a create (INTERLEAVING). The bounds are the first-violation BFS runs in spec/output, and seconds are TLC's rounded wall time; MC.cfg, which is not a hunt config, finished exhaustively with no violation at 50,970 distinct states and diameter 41 (MC_round3.out). All 3 traces pass validation (harness/logs/tlc-*.log), but none reaches fired=true, so the failing branch was never replayed through Trace.tla; it is backed by the reproductions.
